messages:
maya: Heads up — just got an escalated ticket from ACME: p95 and p99 latency jumped ~3x in the last hour. Customer shows many 500s + timeouts. Investigating KV/prefix cache metrics now.
jon: saw the alert too. Any recent deploys to runtime around ~3100M?
sre-bot: deploy-bot rolled out runtime v3.14.7 in us-west-2 at 3112345600 (canary 10%).
manika: I mean anika: I pulled cache stats: global prefix_cache_miss_rate spiked from 4% -> 42% at 3112345620. Evictions/sec also up ~6x.
liam: that smells like a warmup/entropy event — maybe a header explosion or new client header pattern generating unique keys. Any change in SDK header behavior?
support: customer said they started sending a new "X-Request-Tag" with high cardinality around the time of the spike. They rolled that out on their side ~3112345585.
maya: ok that's consistent. High-cardinality header -> cache key entropy -> warmup + thrash. Can we confirm key breakdown?
manika: here's a quick query snippet I ran: 
```
SELECT prefix, count(distinct cache_key_hash) as keys, evictions
FROM kv_prefix_stats
WHERE ts > 3112345500 AND ts < 3112345700
GROUP BY prefix
ORDER BY keys DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
results show one prefix (client:acme:req-tag) with 1.2M distinct keys in 5m.
jon: ouch. That explains p99 blowouts (cold KV lookups + backend fetch). For immediate mitigation: can we enable prefix-key normalization for that tenant or drop that header from cache key?
liam: we can push a hotfix config to normalize/strip high-card headers in the routing layer for acme tenant. Also suggest enabling a TTL-based eviction for that prefix (short TTL) to avoid constant backend hits.
anika: I can push a config change to the per-tenant cache rules: set max_keys=50k, ttl=15s, and enable coarse-key hashing for prefix "client:acme:*". Want me to apply?
support: customer approved quick mitigation (strip X-Request-Tag from cache key).
maya: do it. Also please toggle canary to 100% for the rule once validated. Keep the runtime deploy at 10% — we don't need to roll back if config handles it.
manika: applying change now -> `PATCH /config/tenant/acme/cache-rules {"strip_headers": ["X-Request-Tag"], "max_keys":50000, "ttl_s":15}`
sre-bot: config change applied on control-plane at 3112345680. Propagated to us-west-2 nodes.
liam: monitoring p95/p99 and miss_rate...
maya: any quick perf numbers?
anika: 5m after change miss_rate for that prefix down to 6%, evictions/sec back to baseline. p95 reduced from 420ms -> 120ms, p99 from 1.6s -> 280ms.
john: (jon) nice. What follow-ups do we want to avoid recurrence?
liam: action items: 1) Add automated detection for sudden prefix cardinality growth (+10x in 5m) with tenant-scoped alerts. 2) Add a circuit-breaker to stop counting high-card headers into cache keys (opt-out rule). 3) Update SDK docs: warn about high-cardinality headers and recommend using metadata field that is not part of cache key.
maya: also add a short-term runbook step: when prefix entropy spike detected, suggest strip header, set short TTL, and consider draining requests to fallback model if backend too slow.
support: will update the ticket with mitigation notes for ACME and ask them to change tagging pattern.
sre-bot: created follow-up ticket RM-5243: "auto-detect prefix-cardinality surges + tenant rules" assigned to eng-runtime.
maya: thanks team. Marking this thread resolved for now :thumbsup:
